name: Morphea (Localized Scleroderma)

criteria.description: Presence of one or more circumscribed, indurated plaques with skin thickening and sclerosis
Skin biopsy showing dermal fibrosis with thickened collagen bundles and loss of adnexal structures
No clinical or laboratory evidence of systemic sclerosis
Presence of antinuclear antibodies (ANA) may be supportive but not diagnostic

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two major criteria including clinical presentation and histopathology, with absence of systemic involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by biopsy; systemic sclerosis must be excluded

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized sclerotic plaques with skin induration
Hypopigmented or hyperpigmented patches with violaceous border
searchTerms: light or dark skin patches with purple border
hypo- or hyperpigmented areas with violaceous edges

common.symptomName: Mild pruritus or tenderness over lesions
searchTerms: mild itching or soreness on plaques

common.symptomName: Restricted joint mobility adjacent to plaques
searchTerms: stiff joints adjacent to skin lesions

common.symptomName: Erythematous or violaceous border around plaques
searchTerms: red or purple border around plaques
erythematous or violaceous edges on skin patches

occasional.symptomName: Subcutaneous tissue involvement causing deeper induration

searchTerms: mild joint pain near affected skin

rare.symptomName: Joint contractures due to deep tissue fibrosis
searchTerms: joint stiffness from deep tissue scarring
limited joint movement from tissue tightening
eye inflammation like episcleritis or uveitis

laboratory: Possible positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) in 30-50% of cases
Negative systemic sclerosis specific antibodies (anti-Scl-70, anti-centromere)
imaging: MRI may show dermal and subcutaneous thickening
Ultrasound can demonstrate skin and soft tissue fibrosis
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible HLA associations
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating thickened collagen bundles and loss of adnexal structures

distinguishingFeatures: Widespread skin involvement including hands and face
Systemic organ involvement (lungs, kidneys, GI tract)
Predominantly affects genital and perianal skin
White, atrophic plaques with parchment-like texture
Histology shows epidermal thinning rather than dermal fibrosis
Malignant skin tumor with invasive growth
Histopathology shows basal cell carcinoma features
No sclerosis or fibrosis typical of morphea

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin thickening beyond localized plaques
Development of systemic symptoms such as Raynaud phenomenon or organ dysfunction
Ulceration or infection of skin lesions
references: Fisher BA, et al. Morphea: clinical features and treatment. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2023.
Morphea. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2022.
